I just finished the first 3 books of the "Uglies" series by Scott Westerfeld

I read the series several years back, but I remember enjoying it despite the young adult target audience. One thing that really stood out to me was the way the author chose to slightly alter the way people talk to each other. Specifically the hyphenated "adjective-noun" format. Instead of saying "Bread make you fat," they might say "Bread is fat-making." The lenguage choices are reminiscent of the "new-speak" concept from 1984.

It's a coherent, easy read that lightly touches on many of the same concepts seen in the dystopian Huxley and Orwell novels. The kind of thing id probably want my kid to read before diving into heavier novels like Brave New World. Overall, would recomend.
